text: Making SQL Server available in a second region has meant real infrastructure work — Always On, log shipping, careful failover planning. Cosmos DB was designed to make global distribution a configuration change, not a project.

Adding a region through the portal, CLI, or SDK kicks off background replication — once it completes, that region serves reads, and writes if enabled, automatically kept in sync. There's no manual seeding or separate backup-and-restore step.

By default, one region is the write region and the rest are synced read replicas with automatic failover. Multi-region writes let every configured region accept writes simultaneously — an app in Southeast Asia writes locally instead of round-tripping across the globe.

Multi-region writes solve a latency problem, not a correctness one — when two regions can both accept a write to the same item, a conflict becomes possible. Next up: the five consistency levels that govern what a client actually sees.
